sub: Vision, language, and action with LeRobot

inicio.titulo: VLA: robots that see, understand, and act
inicio.lead: How a model looks at a camera, reads a sentence, and returns arm movements. In eight lessons you learn the architecture, pick a model by its license, open real robot data, train and evaluate a policy with LeRobot, and build the checklist to take it into the real world. You don't need a robot.
inicio.capa_alt: Small robot arm picking up a cube on a dark table, next to a laptop.
inicio.aulas_sub: From concept to workbench: what a VLA is, how it works inside, which models exist in Oct/2026, data, training, simulation, the research frontier, and the path to the real world.

itens: People who code a little in Python and want to understand robotics with AI without memorizing acronyms.
People without a robot: the exercises run on data from the Hugging Face Hub and in simulation. The SO-101 arm is optional.
People who need to decide whether a model fits a real use case and want to check license, access, and safety first.

blocos.t: What you'll be able to do
itens: Say whether a system is an LLM, VLM, VLA, or World Action Model, and why.
Pick a model by license, size, and type of access.
Open a robot dataset, train a short policy, and measure its success rate in simulation.
Build the safety checklist and your study plan with dates.
